bib.title: Deep Compression: Compressing Deep Neural Networks with Pruning, Trained Quantization and Huffman Coding

question: Can a trained CNN's storage and inference energy be cut by an order of magnitude through pruning, trained weight sharing and Huffman coding without losing accuracy?
hypothesis: Pruning and trained quantization do not interfere with each other, so combined they give very high compression at unchanged accuracy.
contributions: Three-stage pipeline: pruning, trained quantization (weight sharing), Huffman coding, giving 35x-49x storage reduction
Evaluation on LeNet-300-100, LeNet-5, AlexNet, VGG-16 with no accuracy loss
Benchmarks of pruned FC layers on CPU, GPU and mobile GPU: 3x-4x speedup, 3x-7x energy at batch 1

method.summary: Train a network, prune connections below a magnitude threshold and retrain, cluster remaining weights per layer with 1-D k-means (linear initialization) and fine-tune the shared centroids with grouped gradients, then Huffman-code the weight indices and relative sparse indices. Implemented in Caffe; speed and energy measured on pruned (not quantized) FC layers.
method.task: neural network compression for inference (image classification)

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.preprocessing: accuracy measured without data augmentation (reference from Caffe model zoo)

training.objective: retraining of pruned weights; centroid fine-tuning with gradient summed per cluster (eq 3), k-means WCSS clustering (eq 2)
training.precision: 32-bit float reference; 8-bit conv / 5-bit FC cluster indices (4-bit relative index for AlexNet, 5-bit for others per Tables 2-5)

other.pruning: remove connections with weights below a threshold (threshold value not given); retrain; implemented by a mask on blobs
other.clusters: 256 per conv layer (8 bits), 32 per FC layer (5 bits) for AlexNet/VGG-16
other.index_encoding: relative index difference, 8 bits conv / 5 bits FC per Sec 2 (text and Table 4 give 4 bits for AlexNet); filler zero padding

inference.samples: timing: 4096 input samples averaged per layer; power measured over repeated runs

parameters.kernels: GPU cuBLAS GEMV/GEMM vs cuSPARSE CSRMV/CSRMM; CPU MKL CBLAS GEMV vs MKL SPBLAS CSRMV

other.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce GTX Titan X, Intel Core i7-5930K, NVIDIA Tegra K1 (Jetson TK1)
other.power: nvidia-smi (GPU), pcm-power (CPU), external meter with 15% AC-DC loss, 85% regulator efficiency, 15% peripherals (Tegra)
other.not_benchmarked: quantized/Huffman-coded model, since BLAS libraries lack indirect lookup

metrics.name: Compression rate
metrics.definition: original size / compressed size including sparse index and codebook overhead (eq 1 for quantization)

metrics.name: Layer time
metrics.definition: average time per input sample over 4096 samples for FC6-FC8; GPU excludes cudaMalloc/cudaMemcpy

metrics.name: Energy
metrics.definition: power x time, normalized to CPU

eval.protocol: Single reported value per cell; no seeds or variance stated.

results.claim: AlexNet storage falls 35x (240MB to 6.9MB) with unchanged top-1 error
results.setup: AlexNet Caffe model, ILSVRC-2012, pruning+trained quantization (8-bit conv, 5-bit FC)+Huffman, includes index and codebook overhead
results.quote: Our method reduced the storage required by AlexNet by 35×, from 240MB to 6.9MB

results.claim: VGG-16 storage falls 49x (552MB to 11.3MB); top-1 error 31.50% to 31.17%
results.quote: Our method reduced the size of VGG-16 by 49× from 552MB to 11.3MB

results.claim: LeNet-300-100 compressed 40x and LeNet-5 39x on MNIST with no error increase
results.setup: MNIST; LeNet-300-100 error 1.64% to 1.58%; LeNet-5 0.80% to 0.74%
results.table: Table 1, rows LeNet-300-100 Compressed (40×) and LeNet-5 Compressed (39×)

results.setup: AlexNet and VGG-16; magnitude threshold, retrain
results.quote: Pruning reduced the number of parameters by 9× and 13× for AlexNet and VGG-16

results.claim: Pruning+quantization gives 27x on AlexNet (8.9MB); Huffman adds to 35x (6.9MB)
results.setup: AlexNet, Table 7 progression; Table 4 totals 3.7% (27x) and 2.88% (35x)

results.claim: Huffman coding saves a further 20-30% of storage
results.setup: Weight and sparse index distributions of last FC layer of AlexNet
results.quote: Experiments show that Huffman coding these non-uniformly distributed values saves 20% −30% of network storage

results.claim: On AlexNet, compression to 2.88% of original size without accuracy impact; Huffman gives an additional 22%
results.setup: AlexNet, 61M parameters, ref top-1 57.2% / top-5 80.3%; 8-bit conv, 5-bit FC, 4-bit relative index
results.quote: Table 4 shows that AlexNet can be compressed to 2.88% of its original size

results.claim: Pruned FC layers give 3x-4x layerwise speedup at batch size 1
results.setup: FC6/FC7/FC8 of AlexNet and VGG-16; Core i7-5930K, Titan X, Tegra K1; batch 1; pruned sparse layer (CSR), quantized model NOT benchmarked
results.note: Figure 9 caption: 3x CPU, 3.5x GPU, 4.2x mobile GPU on average
results.quote: pruned network layer obtained 3× to 4× speedup over the dense network on average

results.claim: Pruned FC layers use 3x-7x less energy at batch size 1
results.setup: Same setup; energy = power x time, AP+DRAM power; Fig 10 caption gives 7x CPU, 3.3x GPU, 4.2x mobile GPU
results.quote: pruned network layer consumes 3× to 7× less energy over the dense network on average

results.claim: At batch size 64 pruning loses its advantage (e.g. Titan X AlexNet FC6 dense 19.8us vs sparse 94.6us)
results.setup: Titan X, AlexNet FC6, batch 64, cuBLAS gemm vs cuSPARSE csrmm
results.note: Text: 'pruned network no longer shows its advantage'
results.table: Table 8, Titan X rows dense (batch=64) and sparse (batch=64), column AlexNet FC6

results.claim: AlexNet with 8/5 bits has no accuracy loss; 8/4 bits loses 0.01% top-1; 4/2 bits loses 1.99% top-1 and 2.60% top-5
results.setup: AlexNet CONV bits / FC bits, Table 6
results.quote: 4/2 bit quantization resulted in 1.99% and 2.60% loss of accuracy

results.claim: CONV layers need more bits than FC: accuracy drops below 4 bits for CONV, below 2 bits for FC
results.setup: AlexNet, Fig 7 quantization with and without pruning
results.quote:
For CONV layers, accuracy drops signiﬁcantly below 4 bits, while FC layer is more robust: not until
2 bits did the accuracy drop signiﬁcantly

results.claim: Linear centroid initialization beats density and random initialization at all bit widths except 3 bits
results.setup: AlexNet, quantized to 2-8 bits, top-1 and top-5, Fig 8
results.quote:
Linear initialization outperforms the density initialization and random initialization in all
cases except at 3 bits

results.claim: Combined pruning and quantization reaches 3% of original size with no loss; each alone degrades below 8%
results.setup: AlexNet, Fig 6; numbers read from text
results.quote:
But when combined, as shown in the red line, the network can be compressed to 3% of original
size with no loss of accuracy

results.claim: Memory energy: 32-bit DRAM access 640pJ vs SRAM 5pJ vs float add 0.9pJ; 1G connections at 20fps needs 12.8W for DRAM
results.setup: 45nm CMOS; cited figures, source not named in text

results.claim: Prior methods on AlexNet: Fastfood 2-3.7x, Collins&Kohli 4x, SVD 5x with 44.02% top-1
results.table: Table 7, row SVD (Denton et al., 2014), column Compress Rate

limits: Speed and energy are measured only for pruned FC layers, not for the quantized or Huffman-coded model, because cuSPARSE and MKL lack indirect lookup and relative indexing (Sec 6.3, Sec 8).
Pruning loses its advantage at batch size 64 on GPU and CPU (Table 8).
Optimizer, learning rate, epochs, pruning threshold and hardware for training are not stated.
Index width stated as 8 bits conv / 5 bits FC in Sec 2 but 4 bits in Sec 5.2 and Table 4.
Full benefit needs custom kernels or an ASIC (EIE, Sec 8).
Accuracy is without data augmentation; one run per cell.

terms.definition: multiple connections share the same weight so only a codebook and small indices are stored
store the index difference instead of absolute position in sparse format, with filler zeros on overflow
